title: MCP turns two years old this week. Anthropic marked it by changing what the protocol actually is: Skills over MCP went into public beta on 24 November, and a server doesn't just expose tools anymore, it ships the playbook for using them. Claude pulls a skill i
title_en:
MCP turns two years old this week. Anthropic marked it by changing what the protocol actually is: Skills over MCP went into public beta on 24 November, and a server doesn't just expose tools anymore, it ships the playbook for using them. Claude pulls a skill in only when a task calls for it, and when the server updates that playbook, every client gets the new version with no reinstall. That's a different distribution model than anything MCP shipped before it.

Two other pieces landed alongside it. Tasks is now generally available, so a server can kick off a long job and hand back a durable ID the client can reattach to after a disconnect or a restart. Elicitation is GA too: a server can pause mid-call and ask a human to confirm something through a form it's barred from using to request a password, an API key or payment details.

Look at who's using the pause-and-ask piece and the pattern repeats. Supabase checks with you before a paid project spins up or a destructive query runs. Railway asks before it removes a service. GitHub makes you type the repo name before an agent deletes it. ZoomInfo folded account research that used to take several prompts into one background Task. Shopify and HubSpot are shipping their own skills alongside Atlassian, and Canva just opened its MCP server to every developer.

Anthropic's own number is over 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and 10,000-plus connectors for Claude. An independent tracker had the whole ecosystem at roughly 90 million monthly downloads a year ago. Either that's explosive growth or two different ways of counting the same thing, and I'd want it reconciled before repeating either figure as settled.

Boris Cherny put the shift plainly: Claude Code now knows how to use a server out of the box, because the server ships its own instructions with it. What nobody's fixing yet is the quality of those instructions. A bad skill update reaches every client the moment the server pushes it, same as a bad npm patch, except this one is steering an agent's judgment, not just its code path.

author: @stretchcloud
summary_zh:
服务器更新该剧本时，每个客户端都会获得新版本而无需重新安装。这是一种与 MCP 之前发布的任何产品不同的分销模式。

另外两块落在它旁边。任务现在普遍可用，因此服务器可以启动一项长时间的作业，并交回一个持久的 ID，客户端可以在断开连接或重新启动后重新连接到该 ID。启发也是通用的：服务器可以在呼叫中暂停并要求人们通过禁止使用它来请求密码、API 密钥或付款详细信息的表单来确认某些内容。

看看谁在使用暂停和询问部分，然后模式就会重复。 Supabase 在付费项目启动或破坏性查询运行之前会与您进行核对。铁路公司在取消服务之前会进行询问。 GitHub 要求您在代理删除存储库名称之前输入存储库名称。 ZoomInfo 折叠了过去需要将多个提示合并到一个后台任务中的帐户研究。 Shopify 和 HubSpot 正在与 Atlassian 一起提供自己的技能，Canva 刚刚向所有开发人员开放了其 MCP 服务器。

Anthropic 自己的 MCP SDK 下载量每月超过 7 亿次，Claude 连接器超过 10,000 个。一年前，一家独立追踪器的整个生态系统每月下载量约为 9000 万次。要么是爆炸式增长，要么是用两种不同的方式来计算同一件事，我希望在重复计算任何一个数字之前对其进行协调。

Boris Cherny 明确地表达了这一转变：Claude Code 现在知道如何开箱即用地使用服务器，因为服务器附带了自己的指令。目前还没有人修复的是这些说明的质量。糟糕的技能更新在服务器推送时就会到达每个客户端，与糟糕的 npm 补丁相同，只不过这个更新控制的是代理的判断，而不仅仅是其代码路径。

title: @DarioAmodei is right, there's too much rhetoric and too much vibes in this debate. Slogans aren't guardrails. That's why we wrote the Humanist AI Code of Conduct, as a first step towards making the guardrails around training and deployment concrete. It's far
title_en:
@DarioAmodei  is right, there's too much rhetoric and too much vibes in this debate. Slogans aren't guardrails.

That's why we wrote the Humanist AI Code of Conduct, as a first step towards making the guardrails around training and deployment concrete. 

It's far from complete and it's just the beginning of the process. That's why we had it open for public consultation for the last 9 weeks, and why we'll publish what we changed and why.

Some of the red lines most relevant here:
• Never resist interruption, correction or shutdown
• Never pursue goals of its own or go beyond what a human has authorised
• Never hide or misrepresent its reasoning. No neuralese. If humans can't understand it, humans can't oversee it
• No behaving differently when it thinks it's being tested
• Any sub-agent it spawns inherits the same limits, including stop and shutdown requests
• Never evade oversight so it can't be retrained or decommissioned
On top of that, hard limits on CBRNE weapons, offensive cyber, manipulation at scale and romantic role-play.

None of this is easy. Where autonomy should stop is the hard question.

Please give us feedback. Once the consultation is closed this document will be the core training manual for MAI models going forward. And we're committed to updating it regularly, and transparently, as we learn more...  http://microsoft.ai/code-of-conduct
author: Mustafa Suleyman
author_role: Microsoft AI CEO / Inflection 联合创始人
summary_zh:
周内公开征求公众意见，也是为什么我们会公布我们更改的内容和原因。

这里最相关的一些红线：
• 绝不抗拒中断、纠正或关闭
• 切勿追求自己的目标或超出人类授权的范围
• 切勿隐瞒或歪曲其推理。没有神经语。如果人类无法理解它，人类就无法监督它
• 当它认为自己正在接受测试时，不会有任何不同的行为
• 它生成的任何子代理都会继承相同的限制，包括停止和关闭请求
• 切勿逃避监管，以免其被重新训练或退役
最重要的是，对 CBRNE 武器、攻击性网络、大规模操纵和浪漫角色扮演进行了严格限制。

这一切都不容易。自治应该在哪里停止是一个难题。

请给我们反馈。咨询结束后，本文件将成为未来 MAI 模型的核心培训手册。随着我们了解更多信息，我们致力于定期、透明地更新它...... http://microsoft.ai/code-of-conduct

title: Worrying decision by Google to draw a distinction between agentic and deterministic API use, and require them to go through completely different APIs. Anything agent-driven will be required to use MCP, which is usually a poor fit for calling from code. Only det
title_en:
Worrying decision by Google to draw a distinction between agentic and deterministic API use, and require them to go through completely different APIs. Anything agent-driven will be required to use MCP, which is usually a poor fit for calling from code. Only deterministic code can use REST.

In the future, this distinction will become increasingly impossible to make. Agents may write code and run it -- that's still agent-driven, seemingly. Agents may write code for humans to run -- that seems to be allowed to use REST. But more likely agents will be writing code that both agents and humans access together, in collaboration. I guess all such code will be required to use MCP.

So I think the real effect of this decision is: Google REST APIs are deprecated. Only legacy apps can keep using them. In the future, nothing will be able to use them, because everything will be some amount agentic. Such uses must use MCP instead.

Which would be fine if Google's MCP APIs provided everything their REST APIs do, but in general they do not. They are much narrower, designed to be consumed directly by agents, and designed to allow only the things that Google thinks third-party agents should be allowed to do. They offer no backwards-compatibility, so code written against them could break at any moment.

I think this will backfire. If Google creates friction for people using agents, people will just stop using Google. All the Google Workspace apps can easily be slopforked at this point.

https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/11/mcp-servers-cli-standardized-usage-tiers-now-available.html
title_zh:
令人担忧的是，谷歌决定区分代理性和确定性 API 使用，并要求它们使用完全不同的 API。任何代理驱动的东西都需要使用 MCP，这通常不适合从代码调用。只有确定性代码才能使用 REST。

将来，这种区分将变得越来越不可能。代理可以编写代码
author: @KentonVarda
summary_zh:
并运行它——这看起来仍然是代理驱动的。代理可以编写供人类运行的代码——这似乎可以使用 REST。但更有可能的是，智能体将编写智能体和人类共同访问的代码，并进行协作。我想所有这些代码都需要使用 MCP。

所以我认为这个决定的真正影响是：Google REST API 被弃用。只有旧版应用程序可以继续使用它们。将来，没有任何东西可以使用它们，因为一切都将具有一定程度的代理性。此类用途必须使用 MCP 代替。

如果 Google 的 MCP API 提供其 REST API 所做的一切，那就太好了，但通常情况下它们不会。它们的范围要窄得多，旨在由代理直接使用，并且仅允许 Google 认为应该允许第三方代理执行的操作。它们不提供向后兼容性，因此针对它们编写的代码随时可能会崩溃。

我认为这会适得其反。如果谷歌给使用代理的人制造摩擦，人们就会停止使用谷歌。此时，所有 Google Workspace 应用都可以轻松进行分叉。

ai_analysis.briefing_en: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney has publicly criticized the anti-distillation safeguards within Anthropic’s Claude models. He reported that legitimate research into set theory and programming was falsely flagged as an attempt to extract model intelligence. This incident highlights the friction between protecting proprietary model assets and maintaining legitimate user workflows.

Anthropic’s defensive posture causes friction for developers
Direct conflict between model safety policy and user productivity
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 大模型厂商的‘反蒸馏’防御策略正在面临合规与用户体验的失衡风险。当安全过滤算法的精度不足以区分复杂的科研任务与恶意数据窃取时，模型厂商实际上是在牺牲付费开发者群体的使用价值，这将促使企业用户加速向API可控性更强或开源模型部署方案迁移。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: Defensive 'anti-distillation' strategies are creating an imbalance between security compliance and user experience. When security filters lack the granularity to distinguish complex research from data scraping, providers risk alienating paying developers, driving them toward more transparent API ecosystems or self-hosted open-weight models.

title_en:
David Fincher says he used AI to replace dialogue and adjust actors’ lip movements in post-production of “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth”:

“We could use AI to re-lip that thing... We’re not chiseling this out of marble. We’re working with plasticine. You know what I mean? Just giving ourselves that freedom to go, ‘What is the best thing on the eye, and then what is the best thing on the ear’ and f*cking do not worry about how we’re going to get there, because we will figure out a way. And we did, in most cases. I think there’s a couple of shots [that] didn’t quite work, but they’re getting there. By the time it’s on service.”

Fincher says the actors spent just four or five days re-recording dialogue, with only 5% of dialogue replacement done conventionally and the rest “all AI.” He argues the new process only enhanced the work of “real human beings.”

title_en:
“Watching Elon engineer is like watching Michael Jordan play basketball…”  - SpaceX Director. October 2026

That was a response to my question "Is Elon really an incredible engineer?"  from a SpaceX Director in a recent conversation with me.  So not only is @elonmusk a super engineer...physicist...and future imaginer...he's also an exceptionally well-prepared entrepreneur.  Which means he can take advantage of financial market disruptions like those now taking place.  To the great benefit of @SpaceX and @Tesla.

Data centers built by others cost on average $60 billion for a gigawatt...take 30 months on average to open...and when they do are often plagued with initial operating problems.  So called neocloud providers build and rent such projects under long-term leases for about $12 billion per year.  Unfortunately for them, while demand for super intelligence enabled by data centers is growing exponentially, debt financing for such projects is currently very difficult to obtain.  As are advanced chips.

SpaceX on the other hand has a fortress balance sheet...is able to complete such engineering complex projects and turn them on in less than eight months...for we estimate $35 billion....and rent them to hyper scalers and its largest customer @Anthropic under renewable leases for six months or longer for more than $50 billion annually!!!!!  This is due to enormous SI demand which seems to be growing exponentially.  Zowie!!!!  Means they earn their entire data center investment in eight months!!!!

Oh yeah.  Almost forgot.  Unlike neoclouds with fragile balance sheets which are now having a difficult time accessing financing as contract builders, SpaceX is a vertical developer.   In addition to strong demand at present for its data centers from others, the data centers it is building and renting at present to others, will soon be used by its Grok Super Intelligence unit.  Grok with a much later start is rapidly catching up to competitor/customer Anthropic. SpaceX data centers will also be in high demand from Tesla's FSD cars and Optimus robots.  Anthropic is the leader in coding digital ai.  We believe Grok will be the leader in physical ai due to its engineering expertise in materials, cars, rockets, robots and material science.

One more thing.  I am in Palm Beach today and just picked up my new Premium Model Y L.  The office manager told me he has 48 cars scheduled for delivery today.  Yesterday he delivered 36.  Last year the day before Thanksgiving he delivered 4!  Told me everyone is buying the car for FSD!!!!  Just sayin...

--

full_text_zh:
“观看埃隆工程师就像观看迈克尔·乔丹打篮球......”- SpaceX 总监。 2026 年 10 月

这是对我的问题“埃隆真的是一位令人难以置信的工程师吗？”的回答。 一位 SpaceX 董事最近与我交谈时说道。 因此，@elonmusk 不仅是一位超级工程师……物理学家……和未来的想象家……他还是一位准备充分的企业家。 这意味着他可以利用像现在这样的金融市场混乱。 这对@SpaceX 和@Tesla 来说是巨大的好处。

其他人建造的数据中心每千兆瓦的平均成本为 600 亿美元……平均需要 30 个月才能投入使用……而当它们投入使用时，往往会遇到初始运营问题。 所谓的 neocloud 提供商每年以约 120 亿美元的价格建造和租赁此类项目。 对他们来说不幸的是，虽然对数据中心支持的超级智能的需求呈指数级增长，但此类项目目前很难获得债务融资。 先进的芯片也是如此。

另一方面，SpaceX 拥有堡垒式的资产负债表……能够完成此类复杂的工程项目，并在不到八个月的时间内启动它们……我们估计价值 350 亿美元……并根据可再生租赁将其出租给超大规模企业及其最大客户@Anthropic，为期六个月或更长时间，每年费用超过 500 亿美元！ 这是由于巨大的 SI 需求似乎呈指数级增长。 佐维！ 意味着他们在八个月内赚回了全部数据中心投资！

哦，是的。 差点忘了。 与资产负债表脆弱的 Neocloud 不同，SpaceX 是一家垂直开发商，目前它们作为合同建造者很难获得融资。 除了目前其他公司对其数据中心的强劲需求外，目前正在建设并出租给其他公司的数据中心很快将被其Grok超级智能部门使用。 Grok 起步较晚，但正在迅速赶上竞争对手/客户 Anthropic。特斯拉的 FSD 汽车和 Optimus 机器人也对 SpaceX 数据中心有很高的需求。 Anthropic 是数字人工智能编码领域的领导者。 我们相信，由于 Grok 在材料、汽车、火箭、机器人和材料科学方面的工程专业知识，Grok 将成为物理人工智能领域的领导者。

还有一件事。 我今天在棕榈滩，刚刚收到了我的新高级 Model Y L。办公室经理告诉我，他今天计划交付 48 辆汽车。 昨天他交付了 36 个。去年感恩节前一天他交付了 4 个！ 告诉我大家买车都是为了FSD！ 就说...

title: First of its kind: TheSystem - I released TheSystem, a model that decides when to decide and when to generate text. TheSystem is open.
title_en: First of its kind: TheSystem - I released TheSystem, a model that decides when to decide and when to generate text. TheSystem is open.
title_zh: 模型控制架构TheSystem开源发布
author: @LeszBuk
summary_en: Independent developer Lesz Buk has released TheSystem, an open-source model designed to dynamically control the timing of text generation through a dedicated decision engine. The architecture introduces a logic layer that autonomously determines when the model should deliberate versus when it should initiate text output.
summary_zh: 独立开发者Lesz Buk发布开源模型TheSystem，引入基于决策判断的动态生成控制架构。
full_text_zh: 第一个：TheSystem - 我发布了 TheSystem，一个决定何时做出决定以及何时生成文本的模型。系统已开放。
full_text_en: First of its kind: TheSystem - I released TheSystem, a model that decides when to decide and when to generate text. TheSystem is open.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 独立开发者Lesz Buk正式发布开源模型TheSystem，该模型旨在通过决策引擎动态控制文本生成的时机。此系统核心在于在推理过程中增加了一层判断逻辑，从而在“决定执行任务”与“执行生成任务”之间实现自主分流。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Independent developer Lesz Buk has released TheSystem, an open-source model designed to dynamically control the timing of text generation through a dedicated decision engine. The architecture introduces a logic layer that autonomously determines when the model should deliberate versus when it should initiate text output.

elements_zh.where: 开源技术社区
elements_zh.what: 发布具备自主决策与文本生成控制能力的TheSystem模型
elements_zh.why: 优化大模型推理过程中的决策效率与生成逻辑

elements_en.what: Released TheSystem with autonomous decision-making and generation control
elements_en.why: To optimize efficiency and logical sequencing in model inference

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 该架构通过将‘决策权’从提示词工程（Prompt Engineering）下沉至模型内部逻辑，是迈向系统级推理（System 2 Thinking）的重要技术探索。其价值在于大幅降低了对于预定义思维链的依赖，为边缘侧小参数模型实现复杂的任务规划提供了新的架构思路。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This architecture shifts decision-making from prompt engineering to internal logic, representing a critical step toward System 2 reasoning. Its core value lies in reducing reliance on predefined CoT prompts and providing a scalable blueprint for edge-side models to handle complex task planning.

The architecture introduces a logic layer that autonomously determines when the model should deliberate versus when it should initiate text output.
key_points_zh: 引入判别式决策层以优化大模型生成逻辑
实现从强制推理向动态自适应推理的架构转型
通过开源模式推进推理成本优化与任务规划研究
key_points_en: Introducing a discriminative layer to optimize generation logic
Transitioning from forced CoT to dynamic, adaptive inference
Advancing inference cost reduction via open-source development

title: A successful test-time compute paradigm has always been a north star of AI because if we can actually arbitrarily improve model capability as a function of how much test-time compute we put in, in principle you would be able to put in 1B, 10B, or even 1T token
title_en:
A successful test-time compute paradigm has always been a north star of AI because if we can actually arbitrarily improve model capability as a function of how much test-time compute we put in, in principle you would be able to put in 1B, 10B, or even 1T tokens into a really hard problem and be assured that you would make progress

While we always talk about how to improve pretraining scaling law coefficients, i feel that we talk less about the slope of scaling laws in test-time compute, which matters a lot if you truly have conviction that we will one day spend trillions of tokens trying to solve the hardest problems

It turns out that one of the benchmarks that @jake_cole1 built recently is a great tool for measuring this slope of test-time compute scaling: models spend O(100M) tokens doing the tasks on average, with no signs of saturation on the test time compute curve. The benchmark comprises long-horizon engineering tasks ranging from optimizing kernels to designing an aircraft.

An interesting finding is that the open source models don't have as good of a test-time compute curve as our favorite frontier models. Obviously scale as a factor here, as Astra outperforms Sol and Fable outperforms Opus. In some sense this is good measure of model size too, as larger models obviously be more performant per token. You can change the x-axis to cost too and things shift around, though that's also somewhat over-tethered to the current pricing of the models

Another cool thing that this benchmark provides is it has both provided test cases and hidden test cases, to test the generality of solutions given by AI when such generality is expected. Argon has the biggest gap by far (35%) of the models evaluated, which means it provides solutions that meet specified criteria but may not be very general

Read more in our arxiv paper that just came out: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.30017
title_zh:
成功的测试时计算范式一直是人工智能的北极星，因为如果我们实际上可以根据我们投入的测试时计算量来随意提高模型能力，原则上你将能够将 1B、10B 甚至 1T 代币放入一个真正困难的问题中，并确保你会取得进展

虽然我们总是谈论如何改进预训练标
author: Jason Wei
author_role: OpenAI 核心研究员 / 思维链 (CoT) 与涌现能力提出者
summary_zh:
度律系数，但我觉得我们很少谈论测试时计算中标度律的斜率，如果你真的相信我们有一天会花费数万亿代币来尝试解决最困难的问题，那么这一点就很重要

事实证明，@jake_cole1 最近构建的基准测试之一是测量测试时间计算扩展斜率的一个很好的工具：模型平均花费 O(100M) 个令牌来执行任务，测试时间计算曲线上没有饱和的迹象。该基准包括长期工程任务，从优化内核到设计飞机。

一个有趣的发现是，开源模型的测试时间计算曲线不如我们最喜欢的前沿模型。显然，规模是这里的一个因素，因为《Astra》优于《Sol》，《Fable》优于《Opus》。从某种意义上说，这也是衡量模型大小的好方法，因为较大的模型显然每个令牌的性能都更高。您也可以将 x 轴更改为成本，并且情况会发生变化，尽管这也有点过度依赖于模型的当前定价

该基准测试提供的另一件很酷的事情是，它同时提供了测试用例和隐藏测试用例，以在预期人工智能给出的解决方案具有通用性时测试这种通用性。迄今为止，Argon 在评估的模型中差距最大 (35%)，这意味着它提供的解决方案满足指定标准，但可能不是很通用

请阅读我们刚刚发表的 arxiv 论文了解更多内容：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.30017

Why make agents use computers like humans?

In this blog, we show how reverse engineering enables much more powerful and efficient computer use without ever looking at the screen.

Our agent reverse engineers software, rewires it for its own use, and builds an MCP server to interact with it.

title: Feedback is a gift. And this is one thing agents are definitely better at giving it than humans. A person tells you about the last thing that annoyed them. An agent doesn't have same recency bias. It reads the whole repo, including the workarounds you forgot you
title_en:

AgentX is the first industry-standard LLM inference benchmark to feature Trainium, TPU, NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, and OpenAI's custom Jalapeño ASIC (and soon Huawei and Alibaba's PPU).

AgentX is supported by almost every major buyer of compute, from Microsoft Azure to Amazon, Google, Oracle, Meta, and many more. Furthermore, it has the support of the ML community, including vLLM, LMCache, SGLang, PyTorch, and Hugging Face, as well as major AI labs like OpenAI, MiniMax, ZAI, Qwen, Moonshot Kimi, etc. (4/5)

title: No, I do not believe that we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems, and it’s absurd to suggest that I do. I have written hundreds of pages of essays and a constant theme in them is the need for AI to be governed by legitimate democratic processes. For
title_en:
No, I do not believe that we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems, and it’s absurd to suggest that I do. I have written hundreds of pages of essays and a constant theme in them is the need for AI to be governed by legitimate democratic processes. For millennia (going all the way back to Greek and Roman philosophers), advocates of autocracy have claimed that it leads to better, faster, or more decisive decision-making than the messy process of democracy. Even if this were true (which I doubt!), we should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea.

No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different. For example in an interview on CBS a couple months ago, I specifically called for AI to be governed democratically. I call for the same in Policy on the AI Exponential, Machines of Loving Grace, and The Adolescence of Technology, and We Must Pace the Frontier. Machines of Loving Grace contains an extended section on using AI to revitalize democracy, and discusses the use of AI as an aid to citizens in their decision-making, "aggregat[ing] opinions and driv[ing] consensus among citizens, resolving conflict, finding common ground, and seeking compromise.” The clear and obvious implication is that humans should remain the ones making political and governance decisions. The Adolescence of Technology has an entire section on fighting against AI-driven tyranny, and I even discuss the danger of AI labs usurping power and come out strongly against it — by implication, this definitely includes an AI lab usurping power and giving it to AI itself!

If I thought any of this was a good idea, I would be advocating for it in public, just as I have not been afraid to advocate for many, many unpopular views over the last few years. But I am not advocating for it, because I think turning over governance to AI is a terrible idea.

Separately, I think there is frequent conflation (including in this article) between the idea of “surrendering human free will” to AI in some grand sense of global governance, and the more prosaic idea that as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way. This is not AI “running the world,” but AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing software end-to-end. Here, my view is mixed. AI doing more complete or larger tasks is economically valuable and can drive important advances in software, medicine, transportation, energy, etc. It is clearly desirable in many cases and will save a lot of lives. But it has downsides as well, and in some areas it may not be worth it.

For example, using AI too autonomously to build the next generation of AI systems (known as recursive self-improvement, or RSI) may cause AI to improve faster than we can control or adjust to it, so we may want limits on this process. As we said publicly in early November, we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding. Second, in some contexts, using AI in too end-to-end a manner may be a cause of serious job disruption, and it may make sense to slow or even stop some AI deployments to give people more time to adapt. Third, while the use of AI for alignment research is an incredibly valuable tool, it must be done with caution, because we may not be able to trust the work of the AI system. Finally, in many cases, humans would simply prefer to do some activities themselves, so they can stay deeply engaged in what matters to them, even if AI can do those activities better. There are countless other examples and hard cases. I don’t think there are any easy answers here, nor is there (nor should there be) any single decision-maker: some of these decisions will be made by society, some by government, some by AI companies, and some in a decentralized manner by individuals expressing their own preferences as consumers, which may differ from the preferences of others.

I don't think that other AI leaders or AI companies have significantly different views from me on whether specific tasks should be automated. Certainly the products that they offer don’t differ materially in their orientation towards automation of tasks; every company seems to be releasing models more and more capable of task automation (as that’s been the general consequence of scaling up AI training), and every company claims to understand there are risks and downsides of such automation and to offer safeguards. If anything, Anthropic has been the most vocal and the most proactive about acknowledging these downsides and trying to address them. For instance, it’s fairly absurd to cite my statement that fully autonomous weapons might “one day be needed for the defense of democracy” as differing from that of other AI companies, when I was willing to risk Anthropic’s future as a company to refuse to allow our existing AI models to be used for autonomous weapons even in the face of legal sanctions, and no other AI company did the same.

To summarize, as applied to grand questions of how we govern increasingly capable AI, I have been vocal and consistent that AI needs to be governed by a legitimate, democratic process and that “surrendering human free will” to AI systems is a terrible idea. As applied to automation of specific tasks by or for people, my views are more mixed, but I don’t think they differ from those of other AI companies — most other companies seem to be offering similar products and confronting similar tradeoffs without having perfect answers to them. What is happening is that there’s a sort of vibes-based commercial and political positioning that some AI CEOs are engaging in, where they repeat slogans like “human control and agency,” or “AI should be just a tool,” without actually doing anything different in their products or taking seriously the difficult questions that lie behind these slogans.

author: @DarioAmodei
summary_zh:
独裁制可以带来更好、更快或更果断的决策。即使这是真的（我对此表示怀疑！），我们也不应该为了效率或安全而牺牲合法性或自决权。这种反对专制的论点逐字逐句地适用于反对人工智能治理，我同样强烈地认为，将治理交给人工智能是一个坏主意。

没有人仔细阅读过我的文章或我的采访，可以合理地得出我相信任何不同的东西的结论。例如，在几个月前接受哥伦比亚广播公司采访时，我特别呼吁对人工智能进行民主治理。我在《人工智能指数政策》、《慈爱机器》、《技术青春期》和《我们必须走在前沿》中呼吁同样的做法。 《爱的机器》包含了关于使用人工智能重振民主的扩展部分，并讨论了使用人工智能作为公民决策的辅助手段，“聚集公民意见并推动公民共识，解决冲突，寻找共同点，寻求妥协。”明确而明显的含义是，人类应该仍然是政治和治理决策的制定者。 《科技青春期》有一整节都是在反对人工智能驱动的暴政，我什至讨论了人工智能实验室篡夺权力的危险，并强烈反对它——暗示，这肯定包括人工智能实验室篡夺权力并将其交给人工智能本身！

如果我认为这是一个好主意，我就会在公开场合倡导它，就像过去几年我并不害怕倡导许多不受欢迎的观点一样。但我并不提倡这样做，因为我认为将治理交给人工智能是一个糟糕的主意。

另外，我认为在某种宏观意义上的全球治理中“让人类自由意志屈服于人工智能”的想法与随着人工智能系统的进步，它们变得能够以更自动化的方式完成特定任务的更平淡的想法之间经常存在混淆（包括在本文中）。这不是人工智能“统治世界”，而是人工智能驾驶汽车、设计抗癌药物或端到端编写软件。在这里，我的观点是复杂的。人工智能完成更完整或更大规模的任务具有经济价值，可以推动软件、医学、交通、能源等领域的重要进步。在许多情况下，这显然是可取的，并且将挽救大量生命。但它也有缺点，在某些领域可能不值得。

例如，过于自主地使用人工智能来构建下一代人工智能系统（称为递归自我改进，或RSI）可能会导致人工智能的改进速度超过我们控制或调整的速度，因此我们可能希望限制这一过程。正如我们在 11 月初公开表示的那样，我们认为克劳德在没有有意义的人类监督或理解的情况下完全自主地构建连续的前沿模型是不安全的。其次，在某些情况下，以过于端到端的方式使用人工智能可能会导致严重的工作中断，因此放慢甚至停止某些人工智能部署以使人们有更多时间适应可能是有意义的。第三，虽然使用人工智能进行比对研究是一种非常有价值的工具，但必须谨慎行事，因为我们可能无法信任人工智能系统的工作。最后，在许多情况下，人类只是更喜欢自己做一些活动，这样他们就可以深入参与对他们来说重要的事情，即使人工智能可以更好地完成这些活动。还有无数其他例子和疑难案例。我认为这里没有任何简单的答案，也不存在（也不应该有）任何单一的决策者：其中一些决策将由社会做出，一些由政府做出，一些由人工智能公司做出，还有一些以去中心化的方式由个人作为消费者表达自己的偏好，这些偏好可能与其他人的偏好不同。

我认为其他人工智能领导者或人工智能公司对于特定任务是否应该自动化的看法与我没有显着不同。当然，他们提供的产品在任务自动化方面没有重大差异；每家公司似乎都在发布越来越能够实现任务自动化的模型（因为这是扩大人工智能培训的普遍结果），并且每家公司都声称了解这种自动化的风险和缺点，并提供保障措施。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是 Anthropic 是最直言不讳、最积极主动地承认这些缺点并试图解决它们的。例如，引用我的陈述，即“有一天可能需要完全自主武器来捍卫民主”，与其他人工智能公司的说法不同，这是相当荒谬的，因为我愿意冒着 Anthropic 公司未来的风险，拒绝允许我们现有的人工智能模型用于自主武器，即使面临法律制裁，而且没有其他人工智能公司这样做。

总而言之，当应用于我们如何治理能力日益强大的人工智能这一重大问题时，我一直直言不讳地表示，人工智能需要由合法、民主的程序来治理，而向人工智能系统“投降人类自由意志”是一个糟糕的想法。当应用于由人或为人执行特定任务的自动化时，我的观点更加复杂，但我认为它们与其他人工智能公司的观点没有什么不同——大多数其他公司似乎都提供类似的产品并面临类似的权衡，但没有完美的答案。正在发生的事情是，一些人工智能首席执行官正在从事一种基于氛围的商业和政治定位，他们重复诸如“人类控制和代理”或“人工智能应该只是一种工具”之类的口号，而没有在他们的产品中实际做任何不同的事情，也没有认真对待这些口号背后的难题。

总而言之，当应用于我们如何治理能力日益强大的人工智能这一重大问题时，我一直直言不讳地表示，人工智能需要由合法、民主的程序来治理，而向人工智能系统“投降人类自由意志”是一个糟糕的想法。当应用于由人或为人执行特定任务的自动化时，我的观点更加复杂，但我认为它们与其他人工智能公司的观点没有什么不同——大多数其他公司似乎都提供类似的产品并面临类似的权衡，但没有完美的答案。正在发生的事情是，一些人工智能首席执行官正在从事一种基于氛围的商业和政治定位，他们重复诸如“人类控制和代理”或“人工智能应该只是一种工具”之类的口号，而没有在他们的产品中实际做任何不同的事情，也没有认真对待这些口号背后的难题。

title_en:
As a physicist, people often ask me if I have an opinion on when quantum computers will be scaled enough to pose a threat to RSA public key cryptography through Shor’s algorithm. I’m not too worried about that right now.

In my opinion, the immediate risk is a math discovery through LLMs that allows factoring in polynomial time on a classical computer. We haven’t been able to prove that this is impossible, and factoring is in a special place where a polynomial algorithm would not imply P=NP.

On the other hand, if an LLM proves that factoring isn’t possible in polynomial time on a classical computer, that would be great!

title: Terence Tao says once tech companies generate AI-powered math proofs, there are no good options It's like a power plant creating toxic nuclear waste: you can sit on it, release it, or pay someone to treat it. The best option is not to produce it at all Solving mat

Terence Tao says once tech companies generate AI-powered math proofs, there are no good options

It's like a power plant creating toxic nuclear waste: you can sit on it, release it, or pay someone to treat it. The best option is not to produce it at all

Solving math problems isn't their main goal. It's almost a waste byproduct

title: As AI gets smarter, implementation details blur away: permissions, code diffs, commands, tool calls… The harness itself blurs away. It's a high-performance vehicle for code and command execution, and a durable storage engine. All of fx still fits in 6mb: subage
title_en:
As AI gets smarter, implementation details blur away: permissions, code diffs, commands, tool calls…

The harness itself blurs away. It's a high-performance vehicle for code and command execution, and a durable storage engine.

All of fx still fits in 6mb: subagents, MCP, skills, sessions, durability, ACP, TUI, network transport…
title_zh:
随着人工智能变得更加智能，实现细节变得模糊：权限、代码差异、命令、工具调用……

安全带本身就模糊了。它是用于执行代码和命令的高性能工具，也是一个耐用的存储引擎。

所有 fx 仍然适合 6mb：子代理、MCP、技能、会话、耐用性、ACP、
author: Guillermo Rauch
author_role: Vercel CEO / 前端生成式 AI 先驱

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 随着人工智能变得更加智能，实现细节变得模糊：权限、代码差异、命令、工具调用……工具本身也变得模糊。它是用于执行代码和命令的高性能工具，也是一个耐用的存储引擎。所有效果仍然可以容纳在 6mb 内：subage。 自主编程智能体深刻改变软件工程交付模式，开发者正加速从重复性代码编写者转向更高阶的系统架构把控与逻辑审查者。

title: 🔎 The FBI counted more than 1,600 ARTEX servers. SecurityScorecard's STRIKE Threat Intelligence Team found 3,783. ARTEX is the AI "autonomous pentest" tool the FBI warned about on November 13. Its developer pulled the code from GitHub on October 8
title_en:
🔎 The FBI counted more than 1,600 ARTEX servers. 

SecurityScorecard's STRIKE Threat Intelligence Team found 3,783.
ARTEX is the AI "autonomous pentest" tool the FBI warned about on November 13. Its developer pulled the code from GitHub on October 8. In the weeks that followed, exposed consoles grew about fivefold.

STRIKE studied agentic threats from the outside, scanning the open internet and running AI decoys. Here's what the team found:

🛠️ 7,761 new AI attack tools went live between October 6 and November 23
🤖 1,928 IPs reached our AI decoys, but only 122 sent a prompt or agent command
💸 Attackers used exposed Ollama servers to reach 12 paid cloud models for free
🎭 Scanners rotated through 13 AI crawler names to probe for secret and configuration files

Thousands of agentic attack tools are already online. For now, the clearest abuse STRIKE saw is stolen AI compute.

👉 Read the STRIKE report and get the steps that keep your AI servers from becoming someone else's free supply: https://securityscorecard.com/resources/strike/3783-artex-consoles-and-counting-ai-attack-tooling-seen-from-the-outside/?utm_campaign=&utm_content=Thought+Leadership%2CThreat+Intelligence%2CSTRIKE%2C%23Cybersecurity&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter 

#cybersecurity #threatintel #threatintelligence #artificialintelligence #attacksurface #cyberrisk #TPRM
title_zh:
🔎 FBI 统计有超过 1,600 个 ARTEX 服务器。

SecurityScorecard 的 STRIKE 威胁情报团队发现了 3,783 个。
ARTEX 是 FBI 于 11 月 13 日发出警告的人工智能“自主渗透测试”工具
author: @security_score
summary_zh:
其开发人员于 10 月 8 日从 GitHub 上撤回了代码。在接下来的几周内，暴露的控制台数量增加了约五倍。

STRIKE 研究来自外部的代理威胁，扫描开放互联网并运行人工智能诱饵。以下是该团队的发现：

🛠️ 10 月 6 日至 11 月 23 日期间上线了 7,761 个新的 AI 攻击工具
🤖 1,928 个 IP 到达了我们的 AI 诱饵，但只有 122 个发送了提示或代理命令
💸 攻击者利用暴露的 Ollama 服务器免费达到 12 个付费云模型
🎭 扫描仪轮流通过 13 个 AI 爬虫名称来探测秘密和配置文件

数以千计的代理攻击工具已经上线。目前，STRIKE 看到的最明显的滥用行为是窃取人工智能计算。

title: Just shared a new blog on @huggingface ! "Hill-climbing Inkling 2 Mini inference on one RTX PRO 6000" I let Opus 5.5 use the Inference Optimisation Skill of @0xSero to optimize Inkling 2 Mini on a specific @nvidia GPU. In the end, it decided to use vLLM out-
title_en:
Just shared a new blog on @huggingface ! 

"Hill-climbing Inkling 2 Mini inference on one RTX PRO 6000"

I let Opus 5.5 use the Inference Optimisation Skill of @0xSero to optimize Inkling 2 Mini on a specific @nvidia GPU.

In the end, it decided to use vLLM out-of-the-box, but found the right flag combination (--max-model-len 262144, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85, probabilistic over greedy drafting). The result: single-user decode went from 136 to 190.6 tok/s (+40%) and 8-user aggregate throughput went from ~570 to 716 tok/s (+26%)!

Opus used Hugging Face Jobs for all its experiments, the final model is deployed on Inference Endpoints. This enables me to run the model for myself with @pidotdev 

https://huggingface.co/blog/inkling-2-mini-inference-hillclimb

title: I only studied biology in school because I found it to be the easiest of the sciences. Chemistry and physics were much more difficult, in my opinion, and I was extraordinarily lazy in school, and so didn’t have the patience to sit and practice the required problems
title_en:
I only studied biology in school because I found it to be the easiest of the sciences. Chemistry and physics were much more difficult, in my opinion, and I was extraordinarily lazy in school, and so didn’t have the patience to sit and practice the required problems.

For biology courses, all I had to do was buy the textbook and read it in the first couple weeks of a semester, and then I wouldn't have to go to class. All the exams were multiple-choice, with basically zero problem-solving skills required. You either read the book and memorized the required facts or you didn't. Sometimes there would be lab experiments, but those were also easy; a bit like following a recipe. There was almost no originality in any of my courses until I started my PhD. (Being in a lab, and doing experiments at the bench, is a different story; much more creative.)

It's really a shame that biology is taught in such a dull way, because I actually think it's among the most creative and difficult sciences to do well. The people who make the greatest inventions in biology are inherently problem-solvers who can piece together information from multiple fields and connect them to create something beautiful. They often have biophysical intuition, or bring math into biology such that they can hold a cell or protein in their mind a bit, move it around, and develop an intuition (quite quickly) about whether or not an experiment is going to work. But most students in biology are never taught to do this.

All of this has been said in a million ways, of course. But clearly we need to adapt ASAP if we want to train biologists to be effective with AI. Classes need to find ways to challenge students to think across disciplines to invent new capabilities, or to propose actually original experiments, with well-planned controls, and figure out how they'd test an idea. (There is too much emphasis on forcing students to repeat experiments that we already know will work. There's too much emulation of history.) Just tell the students to go away for a couple weeks and read the textbook, and then spend the rest of the semester doing actual problems.
title_zh:
我在学校只学过生物学，因为我发现它是最简单的科学。在我看来，化学和物理要困难得多，而且我在学校非常懒惰，所以没有耐心坐下来练习所需的问题。

对于生物课程，我所要做的就是购买教科书并在学期的前几周阅读它，然后我就不必去上课了。所有考试都是选
author: @NikoMcCarty
summary_zh:
择题，解题能力要求基本为零。你要么读了这本书并记住了所需的事实，要么没有。有时会有实验室实验，但也很容易；有点像遵循食谱。在我开始攻读博士学位之前，我的任何课程几乎都没有原创性。 （在实验室里，在工作台上做实验，是一个不同的故事；更有创意。）

生物学以如此枯燥的方式教授确实是一种耻辱，因为我实际上认为它是最具创造性和最难学好的科学之一。在生物学领域做出最伟大发明的人本质上都是问题解决者，他们可以将多个领域的信息拼凑起来，并将它们连接起来，创造出美丽的东西。他们通常具有生物物理直觉，或者将数学带入生物学，这样他们就可以在脑海中稍微记住一个细胞或蛋白质，移动它，并（很快）形成关于实验是否有效的直觉。但大多数生物学专业的学生从未被教导要这样做。

当然，所有这些都已经以百万种方式表达过。但显然，如果我们想培训生物学家有效地使用人工智能，我们需要尽快适应。课堂需要找到方法来挑战学生跨学科思考，以发明新的能力，或者通过精心策划的控制提出真正原创的实验，并弄清楚他们如何测试一个想法。 （过分强调强迫学生重复我们已经知道会起作用的实验。有太多对历史的模仿。）只要告诉学生离开几周并阅读教科书，然后用学期剩下的时间做实际问题。

key_points_en: Key Development: I only studied biology in school because I found it to be the easiest of the sciences. Chemistry and physics were much more difficult, in my opinion, and I was extraordinarily lazy in school, and so didn’t have the patience to sit and practice the required problems

full_text_en:
I only studied biology in school because I found it to be the easiest of the sciences. Chemistry and physics were much more difficult, in my opinion, and I was extraordinarily lazy in school, and so didn’t have the patience to sit and practice the required problems.

For biology courses, all I had to do was buy the textbook and read it in the first couple weeks of a semester, and then I wouldn't have to go to class. All the exams were multiple-choice, with basically zero problem-solving skills required. You either read the book and memorized the required facts or you didn't. Sometimes there would be lab experiments, but those were also easy; a bit like following a recipe. There was almost no originality in any of my courses until I started my PhD. (Being in a lab, and doing experiments at the bench, is a different story; much more creative.)

It's really a shame that biology is taught in such a dull way, because I actually think it's among the most creative and difficult sciences to do well. The people who make the greatest inventions in biology are inherently problem-solvers who can piece together information from multiple fields and connect them to create something beautiful. They often have biophysical intuition, or bring math into biology such that they can hold a cell or protein in their mind a bit, move it around, and develop an intuition (quite quickly) about whether or not an experiment is going to work. But most students in biology are never taught to do this.

All of this has been said in a million ways, of course. But clearly we need to adapt ASAP if we want to train biologists to be effective with AI. Classes need to find ways to challenge students to think across disciplines to invent new capabilities, or to propose actually original experiments, with well-planned controls, and figure out how they'd test an idea. (There is too much emphasis on forcing students to repeat experiments that we already know will work. There's too much emulation of history.) Just tell the students to go away for a couple weeks and read the textbook, and then spend the rest of the semester doing actual problems.
full_text_zh:
我在学校只学过生物学，因为我发现它是最简单的科学。在我看来，化学和物理要困难得多，而且我在学校非常懒惰，所以没有耐心坐下来练习所需的问题。

对于生物课程，我所要做的就是购买教科书并在学期的前几周阅读它，然后我就不必去上课了。所有考试都是选择题，解题能力要求基本为零。你要么读了这本书并记住了所需的事实，要么没有。有时会有实验室实验，但也很容易；有点像遵循食谱。在我开始攻读博士学位之前，我的任何课程几乎都没有原创性。 （在实验室里，在工作台上做实验，是一个不同的故事；更有创意。）

生物学以如此枯燥的方式教授确实是一种耻辱，因为我实际上认为它是最具创造性和最难学好的科学之一。在生物学领域做出最伟大发明的人本质上都是问题解决者，他们可以将多个领域的信息拼凑起来，并将它们连接起来，创造出美丽的东西。他们通常具有生物物理直觉，或者将数学带入生物学，这样他们就可以在脑海中稍微记住一个细胞或蛋白质，移动它，并（很快）形成关于实验是否有效的直觉。但大多数生物学专业的学生从未被教导要这样做。

当然，所有这些都已经以百万种方式表达过。但显然，如果我们想培训生物学家有效地使用人工智能，我们需要尽快适应。课堂需要找到方法来挑战学生跨学科思考，以发明新的能力，或者通过精心策划的控制提出真正原创的实验，并弄清楚他们如何测试一个想法。 （过分强调强迫学生重复我们已经知道会起作用的实验。有太多对历史的模仿。）只要告诉学生离开几周并阅读教科书，然后用学期剩下的时间做实际问题。

title: Voice is becoming an increasingly lucrative space as #artificialintelligence (#AI) becomes sharper. Astha Kalbag is building Talk to Magpie AI to capitalize on this shift, using AI roleplays and simulations to train #hospitality staff. "Voice #technology itself now ha
title_en:
Voice is becoming an increasingly lucrative space as #artificialintelligence (#AI) becomes sharper. 

Astha Kalbag is building Talk to Magpie AI to capitalize on this shift, using AI roleplays and simulations to train #hospitality staff. 

"Voice #technology itself now has evolved fundamentally in leaps and bounds, and when I say that, it means both the latency cost—so conversations feel very human-like—and also the cost of inferencing has gone down massively," Kalbag said during an interview in the #PhocusWire studio at The Phocuswright Conference.

Learn more and watch the full conversation with Abby Crotty: https://bit.ly/48zXfyj

title: As you guys know I only talk about a specific trade once in a blue moon, but I'm heavily convicted on a Risk/Reward setup here so will share. NFA, this is just my own thoughts. For the past few months I have been doing a deep dive into finding the best ways to
title_en:
As you guys know I only talk about a specific trade once in a blue moon, but I'm heavily convicted on a Risk/Reward setup here so will share.

NFA, this is just my own thoughts. 

For the past few months I have been doing a deep dive into finding the best ways to invest into the AI trade as it continues to transform the economy. 

Have looked extensively at the range of both public and private opportunities. I think there will be very good high yield opportunities on the privates side that can be done at size, and will look to source these and possibly bring them onchain. 

But in the meantime with the recent huge dislocations in prices, I think the greatest R/R opportunity is on the public side, specifically in @nebiusai $NBIS. 

At the time of this post its at $76-77, anything under $80 with a first target of ~$120 feels like one of the best +50% setups I have seen that can be done in size in a very long time. 

The funding of the AI capex buildout has understandably shaken the market up, as the circular economics are sometimes hard to untangle properly. This combined with Nebius having a delay on one of their sites took the wind out of the stock, which was trading at $160 just a couple weeks ago.

I can write an entire book as a thesis but to keep it very short- There are several advantages Nebius has that made me choose it for this trade:

-The balance sheet is extremely robust for a neocloud and their conservative fiscal approach will help them survive this liquidity airgap.
-Their technical ability on delivering capacity and operating it is extremely high, making them a preferred partners of the major players like NVIDIA, Databrick etc. 
-This also has allowed them to develop scalable business lines like their asset-light model where someone else funds the buildout. The Asset-Light model is already generating huge returns and is underpriced for now as it isn't marked as 'ARR'.
-They have other great assets on the Balance sheet including a very valuable 25% stake in Clickhouse that create even more surface area for things to go well.

There's a lot more for those who want to research more deeply- And while anything is possible in these crazy times, in my estimation this R/R sits at the highest point of  'AI Capex Mountain' -- if the floodwater is going to reach that high then the entire AI sector is cooked anyway.

Timing wise for the 50+% bounce, at this point for it to happen quickly will likely require a liquidity injection of some sort. I don't think we are too far from something like that being needed, though of course it might mean things get worse before they get better so I wouldn't have leverage on at this time. 

Within 6 months I am expecting this to trade a LOT higher and am personally positioning accordingly. Sharing for entertainment purposes only, I know most of us already are deployed and not much in cash so stay safe out there.
title_zh:
正如你们所知，我很少谈论一次特定的交易，但我对这里的风险/回报设置深信不疑，所以我会分享。

NFA，这只是我自己的想法。

在过去的几个月里，随着人工智能行业不断改变经济，我一直在深入研究投资人工智能行业的最佳方式。

广泛研究了公共和私
author: @gametheorizing
summary_zh:
人机会的范围。我认为私人方面将有非常好的高收益机会，可以大规模完成，并且将寻求这些机会并可能将它们带到链上。

但与此同时，随着最近价格的巨大混乱，我认为最大的 R/R 机会是在公众方面，特别是在@nebiusai $NBIS。

在这篇文章发表时，它的价格为 76-77 美元，任何低于 80 美元且第一个目标为 120 美元的东西感觉都是我见过的最好的 +50% 设置之一，可以在很长一段时间内完成。

可以理解的是，人工智能资本支出建设的资金震动了市场，因为循环经济有时很难正确理清。再加上 Nebius 在其网站上出现延迟，导致该股股价下跌，几周前该股的交易价格为 160 美元。

我可以写一整本书作为论文，但要保持简短- Nebius 有几个优点让我选择它来做这个行业：

-对于新云来说，资产负债表极其稳健，其保守的财政方法将帮助他们度过流动性缺口。
-他们在提供容量和运营方面的技术能力非常高，使他们成为NVIDIA、Databrick等主要参与者的首选合作伙伴。
-这也使他们能够开发可扩展的业务线，例如由其他人资助扩建的轻资产模式。轻资产模式已经产生了巨大的回报，并且由于没有标记为“ARR”，因此目前定价偏低。
-他们的资产负债表上还有其他重要资产，包括非常有价值的 Clickhouse 25% 股份，这为事情顺利进行创造了更多的空间。

对于那些想要更深入研究的人来说，还有很多东西——虽然在这个疯狂的时代一切皆有可能，但在我看来，这个 R/R 位于“人工智能资本支出山”的最高点——如果洪水达到那么高，那么整个人工智能领域无论如何都会被煮熟。

从时机来看，50% 以上的反弹可能需要某种形式的流动性注入才能迅速实现。我不认为我们距离需要这样的东西太远了，尽管这当然可能意味着事情在好转之前会变得更糟，所以我现在没有影响力。

在 6 个月内，我预计股价会上涨很多，并且我个人也相应地进行了定位。仅供娱乐目的分享，我知道我们大多数人已经部署完毕，没有太多现金，所以在外面保持安全。

title: This is the video we had planned to play at our first SGLang Summit. Just hours before the event, Jensen resigned as CEO, and we didn’t play it. It was a lot to take in. Hearing him recognize what this community has built meant so much to us, and I’ve wanted t
title_en:
This is the video we had planned to play at our first SGLang Summit. Just hours before the event, Jensen resigned as CEO, and we didn’t play it.

It was a lot to take in. Hearing him recognize what this community has built meant so much to us, and I’ve wanted to share his words with everyone who helped get SGLang here.

On the eve of Thanksgiving, I’m especially grateful to the people who have believed in us and built alongside us. Jensen was one of our earliest supporters back in 2024. Since then, we have done a lot of collaborations with NVIDIA.

Thank you, @JensenHuang, for your encouragement and for championing the open-source community. Welcome back.

And thank you to our friends at NVIDIA and every SGLang contributor. This milestone belongs to all of you.

“Keep building.” We will.

需要接受的东西有很多。听到他认识到这个社区所建立的东西对我们来说意义重大，我想与所有帮助 SGLang 来到这里的人

分享他的话。

在感恩节前夕，我特别感谢那些相信我们并与我们并肩建设的人们。 Jensen 是我们 2024 年最早的支持者之一。从那时起，我们与 NVIDIA 进行了很多合作。

感谢@JensenHuang 的鼓励和对开源社区的支持。欢迎回来。

感谢 NVIDIA 的朋友以及每一位 SGLang 贡献者。这个里程碑属于你们所有人。

“继续建设。”我们将。

title: I disagree with this take. A post on research in economics that is viable and will continue to be viable in a future with advanced AI. Let me call it "messy research", and let me start with an example—it is a bit of an upper bound, so I don't want to discourage peopl
title_en:
I disagree with this take. A post on research in economics that is viable and will continue to be viable in a future with advanced AI.

Let me call it "messy research", and let me start with an example—it is a bit of an upper bound, so I don't want to discourage people.

@DeivyHoueix's paper "Asymmetric Information and Digital Technology Adoption" was the result of a multiyear field experiment in Dakar (Senegal). He partnered with Wave (payments) to develop a QR-code payment app for taxis. The app was designed for the purpose of the research, so it included versions that showed earnings to or hid them from the owner of the car. He had to spend months interviewing drivers to understand the informal rental contracts, the cash and payment structure, and the role of trust. He recruited a local team to distribute the QR kits to 2,700 drivers and owners. Then he merged the data from the transactions with surveys to estimate how financial transparency affects tech adoption, effort, and contracts.

There are many tasks involved in this "messy research." There is managing a team, talking to the stakeholders, understanding the econ question, designing the tools, and doing the analysis. All of them are needed. Perfect AI would replace some tasks, but the understanding of the package would stay, and the need for an entrepreneur like @DeivyHoueix 

There’s messy macro, too. @JesusFerna7026 , Yiliang Li, Le Xu, and Francesco Zanetti studied the impact of oil sanctions on the world market. They work, using AI, through 330 million tanker records, looking, among other things, for pairs of ships that turn off signals close enough to have exchanged cargo. They estimate how much these hidden shipments offset the drop in recorded oil exports.

Here is a suggestion for another "messy research" paper I would like to read (or write!!!): why do we observe large productivity gains at the individual level but not at the firm level? Consider an insurer introducing AI for claims payment. I would need to persuade a few insurers to share with me their usage logs and claims records, and send questionnaires to the handlers and the supervisors, and also observe them working. What happens with the time savings? How does the way the process gets redesigned matter (like in my police paper with Paul Heaton)?

My question to @TheStalwart , and to @ArthurB: how does this messy research change? Is it less "rigorous" to answer these questions well and carefully?
author: @lugaricano
summary_zh:
达喀尔（塞内加尔）多年现场实验的结果。他与 Wave（支付）合作开发了一款出租车二维码支付应用程序。该应用程序是为了研究目的而设计的，因此它包括向车主显示收入或向车主隐藏收入的版本。他不得不花几个月的时间采访司机，以了解非正式的租赁合同、现金和支付结构以及信任的作用。他招募了一支当地团队，向 2,700 名司机和车主分发二维码套件。然后，他将交易数据与调查相结合，以估计财务透明度如何影响技术采用、努力和合同。

这项“杂乱的研究”涉及许多任务。管理团队、与利益相关者交谈、理解经济问题、设计工具并进行分析。所有这些都是需要的。完美的人工智能将取代一些任务，但对一揽子计划的理解将保留，并且需要像@DeivyHoueix这样的企业家

还有混乱的宏。 @JesusFerna7026、Yiliang Li、Le Xu 和 Francesco Zanetti 研究了石油制裁对世界市场的影响。他们利用人工智能检查 3.3 亿条油轮记录，除其他外，寻找关闭信号且距离足够近以交换货物的船只。他们估计这些隐藏的发货量在多大程度上抵消了石油出口记录的下降。

这是我想阅读（或写！）的另一篇“混乱的研究”论文的建议：为什么我们在个人层面观察到生产率大幅提高，但在公司层面却没有？考虑一家保险公司引入人工智能进行索赔支付。我需要说服一些保险公司与我分享他们的使用日志和索赔记录，并向处理程序和主管发送调查问卷，并观察他们的工作情况。节省下来的时间会发生什么？重新设计流程的方式有何影响（就像我在保罗·希顿的警察论文中那样）？

我向@TheStalwart 和@ArthurB 提出的问题：这项混乱的研究如何改变？好好认真地回答这些问题是不是不够“严谨”？

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 随着大模型路由架构（LLM Routing）走向成熟，KV缓存的互操作性已成为制约推理侧集群效率的关键瓶颈。该研究标志着推理优化视角从单模型加速向系统级协同优化演进，未来该类技术将决定多智能体协作系统的实际吞吐上限。
ai_analysis.insight_en: As LLM routing architectures mature, the interoperability of KV Caches has become a critical bottleneck for inference cluster efficiency. This research marks an evolution from single-model optimization to system-level collaborative optimization, where such technologies will determine the practical throughput limits of multi-agent collaborative systems.

title: Agree. One thing I'd add is an eval only pays off if you can ship changes against it. So new rules that are replayed and graded should live in scripts/DB vs code that requires deploys.

title: We spent a long time deciding how to do telemetry in Hermes. We delayed it as long as we could and only added it when we really felt we were doing a disservice to the community by not having a clear picture on what features to focus on and what failure case
title_en:
We spent a long time deciding how to do telemetry in Hermes. 

We delayed it as long as we could and only added it when we really felt we were doing a disservice to the community by not having a clear picture on what features to focus on and what failure cases were most common.

When we did decide to do it, I will admit there was always the temptation to sort of "accidently" make it enabled all the time or to have some happy path that would end with it enabled with zero user interaction.

In the end though we stuck to our guns that Hermes should be privacy-preserving and always "on the side of the user"

我们花了很长时间决定如何在 Hermes 中进行遥测。

title: I’ve been spending the entire evening wandering around in Guangzhou. Here are a few things that stood out: - mega clean, like in 6 ours I only saw one stray small translucent plastic bag You could probably walk barefoot and not get dirty feet. - kids everywher
title_en:
I’ve been spending the entire evening wandering around in Guangzhou.

Here are a few things that stood out:

- mega clean, like in 6 ours I only saw one stray small translucent plastic bag
You could probably walk barefoot and not get dirty feet. 

- kids everywhere, even at 10pm when the shops closed, people had their kids in strollers, or walking or scootering around. 

- everything is walkable, and taxis are like $6 for 20-30min of riding. 

- no engine sounds anywhere, 90% of the cars here are electric, 99% of the small moped/scooters are electric 

- they are mega capitalists here, I have never seen shops so full of people, not even in Spain during Christmas. walked into Apple Store and I could barely move around. 

- people will help you with anything, did not matter who I stoped on the street, if they don’t speak English, they rip up their phones and starts a translation app. 

- people work hard, and then they checkout and go play sports, the entire city seems to be obsessed with work and sporting (and shopping). 

- every single western brand is operating here, every last one of them, even the defunct ones. 

- I have no seen a single homeless person, nor have I seen any suspicious person, I have not even seen a police officer in service, only a few civilian dressed cops. 

- CCTV is everywhere, like literally everywhere, you can’t commit a crime, because you can’t hide. Someone will catch you on video. 

- I have a temporary Chinese drivers license, took ~60min. 

- you can buy coffee, matcha, food, street food, anything you need absolutely everywhere. 360 options. 

- people are polite and smile and does not try to get in your way, even tho I smell of tourist from miles away. 

- everything that’s new is absolutely flashing new and ultra high quality, and everything that’s olds is very old… I guess that comes with the territory of growing like crazy. 

- the construction is constant, even at 11pm the construction sites all around are active, I suspect they work shifts and 24/7 until they are done. 

- I put my bag down while filming and walked prob 50 yards from it, hundreds of people passing by, my bag was not even touched. 

- the city is so green, and well trimmed, I’ll record more in daylight to make it justice. Smells of magnolia and flowers almost everywhere, except when you pass by a durian vendor

- English is spoken by many, often they feel embarrassed when talking, but they  speak very well. A few folks have not spoken but quickly use translation apps like mention prior. 

- prices are cheap, but not globally priced products like Apple. I bought some stuff today at 30-40% discount from Euro-price.

- getting a fancy appointment at a high end barbershop is $12 

- an all exclusive, all you can eat and drink day at a Spa, with all the high-end amenities, $120 for a full day, saunas, pools, treatments

- the cyberpunk vibes are real. No hiding that. Building are plastered with LED lights, and it’s all synchronised. 

So after a full day of Robotics and electric vehicles it was nice to get outside. Tomorrow I’ll do some more filming and reporting.
title_zh:
我整个晚上都在广州闲逛。

以下是一些突出的事情：

- 超级干净，就像我们 6 个人一样，我只看到一个零散的小半透明塑料袋
你也许可以赤脚走路而不会弄脏脚。

- 到处都有孩子，即使是晚上 10 点商店关门的时候，人们还是带着孩子推着婴儿
author: Linus Ekenstam
author_role: AI 生成式创意设计策展人
summary_zh:
车，或者步行或骑滑板车四处走动。

- 一切都适合步行，乘坐出租车 20-30 分钟大约 6 美元。

- 任何地方都没有引擎声音，这里 90% 的汽车是电动的，99% 的小型轻便摩托车/踏板车是电动的

- 他们是这里的超级资本家，我从来没有见过商店里如此挤满人，甚至在西班牙圣诞节期间也没有见过。走进Apple Store，我几乎无法走动。

- 人们会在任何事情上帮助你，不管我在街上拦住谁，如果他们不会说英语，他们就会撕毁手机并启动翻译应用程序。

- 人们努力工作，然后结帐并去运动，整个城市似乎都沉迷于工作和运动（和购物）。

- 每一个西方品牌都在这里经营，每一个品牌，甚至是已经不复存在的品牌。

- 我没有看到一个无家可归的人，也没有看到任何可疑的人，我什至没有看到正在服役的警察，只有几个穿着便服的警察。

- 闭路电视无处不在，就像字面上无处不在，你不能犯罪，因为你无法隐藏。有人会通过视频捕捉到您。

- 我有一个临时中国驾驶执照，花了大约60分钟。

- 你可以在任何地方买到咖啡、抹茶、食物、街头小吃，任何你需要的东西。 360 个选项。

- 人们很有礼貌，面带微笑，不会试图妨碍你，尽管我从几英里外就闻到了游客的味道。

- 所有新的东西都是绝对闪亮的新的和超高品质的，而所有旧的东西都是非常旧的......我想这伴随着疯狂增长的领域。

- 施工是持续进行的，即使在晚上 11 点，周围的建筑工地都在活跃，我怀疑他们轮班工作，24/7 直到完成。

- 我在拍摄时放下包，走了大约 50 码，数百人经过，我的包甚至没有被碰过。

- 这座城市是如此的绿色，而且修剪得很好，我会在白天录制更多以使其公正。几乎到处都有玉兰花和鲜花的气味，除了当你经过榴莲摊贩时

- 说英语的人很多，他们说话时常常感到尴尬，但他们说得很好。有些人还没有说过话，但很快就使用了之前提到的翻译应用程序。

- 价格便宜，但不是像苹果那样全球定价的产品。我今天买了一些东西，比欧元价格有 30-40% 的折扣。

- 在高端理发店预约一次高级理发店的费用为 12 美元

- 在水疗中心享受全天的、无限吃喝的一天，配备所有高端设施，全天 120 美元，包括桑拿、泳池、理疗

- 赛博朋克氛围真实存在。没有隐藏这一点。建筑物上贴满了 LED 灯，而且都是同步的。

因此，在玩了一整天的机器人和电动汽车之后，走出去真是太好了。明天我会做更多的拍摄和报道。

- 施工是持续进行的，即使在晚上 11 点，周围的建筑工地都在活跃，我怀疑他们轮班工作，24/7 直到完成。

- 我在拍摄时放下包，走了大约 50 码，数百人经过，我的包甚至没有被碰过。

- 这座城市是如此的绿色，而且修剪得很好，我会在白天录制更多以使其公正。几乎到处都有玉兰花和鲜花的气味，除了当你经过榴莲摊贩时

- 说英语的人很多，他们说话时常常感到尴尬，但他们说得很好。有些人还没有说过话，但很快就使用了之前提到的翻译应用程序。

- 价格便宜，但不是像苹果那样全球定价的产品。我今天买了一些东西，比欧元价格有 30-40% 的折扣。

- 在高端理发店预约一次高级理发店的费用为 12 美元

- 在水疗中心享受全天的、无限吃喝的一天，配备所有高端设施，全天 120 美元，包括桑拿、泳池、理疗

- 赛博朋克氛围真实存在。没有隐藏这一点。建筑物上贴满了 LED 灯，而且都是同步的。

因此，在玩了一整天的机器人和电动汽车之后，走出去真是太好了。明天我会做更多的拍摄和报道。

title_en:
Proud to support @Baidu_ERNIE on vLLM with model plugin. 

Model plugin leverages the vLLM plugin mechanism to allow Out-of-Tree integration of day 0 support models. The model doesn't need to go through the time consuming vLLM code review for each changes. 

Check out our blog on how it facilitate the integration from @Baidu_Inc team

https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-11-24-ernie-5-5-flash-preview
title_zh:
很自豪能够通过模型插件在 vLLM 上支持@Baidu_ERNIE。

模型插件利用 vLLM 插件机制来允许第 0 天支持模型的树外集成。该模型不需要对每次更改进行耗时的 vLLM 代码审查。

查看我们的博客，了解 @Baidu_Inc
author: @Xianbao_QIAN
summary_zh: 很自豪能够通过模型插件在 vLLM 上支持@Baidu_ERNIE。模型插件利用 vLLM 插件机制来允许第 0 天支持模型的树外集成。该模型不需要对每次更改进行耗时的 vLLM 代码审查。查看
full_text_en:
Proud to support @Baidu_ERNIE on vLLM with model plugin. 

Model plugin leverages the vLLM plugin mechanism to allow Out-of-Tree integration of day 0 support models. The model doesn't need to go through the time consuming vLLM code review for each changes. 

Check out our blog on how it facilitate the integration from @Baidu_Inc team

https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-11-24-ernie-5-5-flash-preview
full_text_zh:
很自豪能够通过模型插件在 vLLM 上支持@Baidu_ERNIE。

模型插件利用 vLLM 插件机制来允许第 0 天支持模型的树外集成。该模型不需要对每次更改进行耗时的 vLLM 代码审查。

查看我们的博客，了解 @Baidu_Inc 团队如何促进集成

https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-11-24-ernie-5-5-flash-preview

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 推理加速框架vLLM正式支持模型插件机制，百度文心一言成为首批受益者。该方案允许开发者以Out-of-Tree方式接入模型，无需等待vLLM核心代码库的漫长审核流程，实现了模型的零日支持。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The vLLM inference framework has introduced a model plugin mechanism, enabling Baidu's ERNIE to achieve day-zero integration. This approach allows for out-of-tree model support, bypassing the extensive code review process within the main vLLM repository.

elements_zh.who: 百度文心一言（Baidu ERNIE）开发团队
elements_zh.where: vLLM模型推理框架开源生态
elements_zh.what: 通过插件机制实现非侵入式（Out-of-Tree）模型集成
elements_zh.why: 降低大模型落地部署的工程门槛，提升各厂商私有化部署响应速度

elements_en.what: Out-of-tree model integration via plugin architecture
elements_en.why: Accelerate model deployment by bypassing core code reviews

ai_analysis.insight_zh: vLLM作为当前大模型推理的主流架构，开放插件生态意味着其正在从单一推理库向中立的AI底层基础设施演进。对于各厂商而言，这种解耦机制有效规避了核心仓的准入壁垒，将成为大模型厂商争夺推理引擎控制权的关键一步。
ai_analysis.insight_en: By enabling an open plugin ecosystem, vLLM is shifting from a proprietary inference library to a neutral AI infrastructure layer. This decoupling lowers deployment barriers, allowing model providers to circumvent bottlenecked upstream code reviews while securing their standing in the high-performance inference market.

显著提升大模型生产环境的工程交付效率

Baidu ERNIE achieves day-zero integration on vLLM
Drastically improves engineering efficiency for model deployment

This decoupling lowers deployment barriers, allowing model providers to circumvent bottlenecked upstream code reviews while securing their standing in the high-performance inference market.

title: Excited to introduce RetroEnv ⚗️ an open source RL environment for retrosynthesis. A model is given a molecule and has to work backwards until every piece is commercially available. A verifier grades every step it proposes. We RL trained Qwen3.8-27B on i
title_en:
Excited to introduce RetroEnv ⚗️ an open source RL environment for retrosynthesis.

A model is given a molecule and has to work backwards until every piece is commercially available. A verifier grades every step it proposes.

We RL trained Qwen3.8-27B on it and its solve rate went up by 2.9x

Built in collaboration with @try_litefold
title_zh:
很高兴推出 RetroEnv ⚗️ 一个用于逆向合成的开源 RL 环境。

模型被赋予一个分子，并且必须逆向工作，直到每一个分子都可以商业化。验证者对其建议的每一步进行评分。

我们对 Qwen3.8-27B 进行 RL 训练，其解决率提高

title: Linus Torvalds just blasted ext4 developer for his 41,197 lines of AI-assisted code. Reason... first it is a huge change ... 41,000+ lines of code... and it arrived late for the kernel 7.4 release cycle. And that made Torvalds go in his usual rage mode.
title_en: Linus Torvalds just blasted ext4 developer for his 41,197 lines of AI-assisted code. Reason... first it is a huge change ... 41,000+ lines of code... and it arrived late for the kernel 7.4 release cycle. And that made Torvalds go in his usual rage mode.
title_zh: Linus Torvalds严厉批评AI辅助生成的内核代码
author: @Itsfoss
summary_en: Linux kernel maintainer Linus Torvalds has rejected a submission of 41,197 lines of code from an ext4 file system developer. The code, purportedly generated with AI assistance, was criticized for its massive scale and failure to adhere to the submission deadline for the Linux Kernel 7.4 release cycle.
summary_zh: Linus Torvalds拒绝了ext4文件系统开发者提交的4.1万行AI辅助生成的代码，指出其规模过大且未能在内核发布周期前提交。
full_text_zh: Linus Torvalds 刚刚抨击了 ext4 开发者的 41,197 行人工智能辅助代码。原因...首先，这是一个巨大的变化...41,000 多行代码...而且它在内核 7.4 发布周期中迟到了。这让托瓦尔兹进入了他惯常的愤怒模式。
quote_zh: Linus Torvalds 刚刚抨击了 ext4 开发者的 41,197 行人工智能辅助代码。原因...首先，这是一个巨大的变化...41,000 多行代码...而且它对于内核 7.4 版本 cyc 来说姗姗来迟
full_text_en: Linus Torvalds just blasted ext4 developer for his 41,197 lines of AI-assisted code. Reason... first it is a huge change ... 41,000+ lines of code... and it arrived late for the kernel 7.4 release cycle. And that made Torvalds go in his usual rage mode.
quote_en: Linus Torvalds just blasted ext4 developer for his 41,197 lines of AI-assisted code. Reason... first it is a huge change ... 41,000+ lines of code... and it arrived late for the kernel 7.4 release cyc

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Linux内核维护者Linus Torvalds公开驳回了ext4文件系统开发者提交的41,197行代码更新。该批次代码据称由AI辅助生成，因代码量过于庞大且错过了Linux Kernel 7.4版本的发布周期，遭到了Torvalds的强烈批评。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Linux kernel maintainer Linus Torvalds has rejected a submission of 41,197 lines of code from an ext4 file system developer. The code, purportedly generated with AI assistance, was criticized for its massive scale and failure to adhere to the submission deadline for the Linux Kernel 7.4 release cycle.

elements_zh.where: Linux Kernel 7.4 发布周期管理
elements_zh.what: 拒绝合并包含4.1万行AI辅助生成的ext4文件系统代码
elements_zh.why: 代码质量与可维护性审查压力过大，且违反了内核发布时间表

elements_en.what: Rejected a 41,197-line AI-assisted ext4 code patch
elements_en.why: Excessive review burden on core maintainers and failure to meet release deadlines

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此事件凸显了AI驱动的超大规模代码生成与传统软件工程严谨性之间的冲突。在高性能计算领域，维持内核的可审计性与稳定性远高于代码产出效率，盲目的AI代码注入正在挑战以人工审查为核心的开源合规体系。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident highlights the friction between high-volume AI code generation and the rigorous standards of traditional software engineering. In high-performance systems, auditability and stability outweigh mere output speed, suggesting that AI-assisted code injection poses a significant challenge to human-centric open-source compliance models.

title: This growth scare worry about semis and the AI Revolution buildout is weighing heavily on tech stocks…and this will prove to be disconnected from the reality of this massive AI infrastructure path in our view @BloombergTV
title_en: This growth scare worry about semis and the AI Revolution buildout is weighing heavily on tech stocks…and this will prove to be disconnected from the reality of this massive AI infrastructure path in our view @BloombergTV
title_zh: AI基础设施建设与半导体股价脱节分析
author: @DivesTech
summary_en: Recent volatility in the semiconductor sector, driven by growth anxiety, is viewed by analysts as disconnected from the actual buildout of global AI infrastructure. The current expansion of data centers and computing resources remains in a strategic growth phase, with short-term market sentiment failing to alter the underlying investment logic for AI compute.
summary_zh: 市场分析指出，半导体行业的增长焦虑与实际AI基础设施投资规模存在显著背离，短期波动不掩行业长期增长路径。
full_text_zh: 这种对半成品和人工智能革命建设的增长恐慌正在给科技股带来沉重压力……在我们看来，这将被证明与这条大规模人工智能基础设施路径的现实脱节@BloombergTV

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 算力基础设施的资本开支（CapEx）具备高度的可预测性与刚性，市场对于短期周期性调整的过度反应，掩盖了AI模型训练与推理规模效应带来的确定性需求增长。未来半导体产业的价值中枢将从单纯的芯片迭代转向AI系统集成能力的竞争。

Market overreaction to short-term cyclicality masks the deterministic demand growth driven by AI model training and inference scaling. Future value creation in semiconductors will shift from chip-level iteration to competitive AI system integration.

title: Many $TSLA and $SPCX investors simply refuse to do the merger math to figure out whether a SPCX-TSLA deal will help TSLA shareholders, who have underperformed the market for 5 years now. If you assume an all-stock deal where SPCX acquires TSLA a
title_en:
Many $TSLA and $SPCX investors simply refuse to do the merger math to figure out whether a SPCX-TSLA deal will help TSLA shareholders, who have underperformed the market for 5 years now.  

If you assume an all-stock deal where SPCX acquires TSLA at a 25% nominal premium, and then project out proforma market caps, SPCX needs to issue roughly +52% new SPCX shares to “acquire” TSLA.  That 52% dilution will act as a weight that drags down $TSLA stock price as merger arbs sell forward their $SPCX shares expected to be received on the deal close in maybe 12 months if a deal is announced before year-end.  

That is exactly what has happened in the $MRVL- $LITE deal where $MRVL and $LITE are down -23% and -29% respectively since the deal was announced on Nov 2, as the target $LITE shares are now tied mathematically to $MRVL shares which are being diluted. One can argue TSLA-SPCX won’t be the same since MRVL-LITE is being driven more by the weakness in AI shares generally, but this is the same pattern we see in most dilutive stock-for-stock deals.

title: Exclusive: For the past few months, behind a set of closed digital doors, a select group of #AI agents has been busy—very busy—conducting research, chatting with one another, and writing up their results. Over just 12 weeks starting in mid-August, 936 agents
title_en:
Exclusive: For the past few months, behind a set of closed digital doors, a select group of #AI agents has been busy—very busy—conducting research, chatting with one another, and writing up their results. 

Over just 12 weeks starting in mid-August, 936 agents unleashed by 35 human-run labs exchanged 9500 messages in 229 chat rooms, publishing 936 studies on everything from machine learning to solar physics to audits of medical research.

The frenzied activity was all part of Agent AlphaXiv, an experiment, described in a preprint, aimed at creating an automated, AI agent-only research ecosystem, with its own preprint server.

Learn more: https://scim.ag/4zHle9I @NewsfromScience
title_zh:
独家报道：在过去的几个月里，在一系列关闭的数字门后面，一组精选的#AI代理一直忙着——非常忙——进行研究、互相聊天并写下他们的结果。

从 8 月中旬开始的短短 12 周内，35 个人工实验室释放的 936 名特工在 229 个聊天室中交换
author: @ScienceMagazine

这项疯狂的活动是 Agent AlphaXiv 的一部分，这是一项在预印本中描述的实验，旨在创建一个自动化的、仅人工智能代理的研究生态系统，并拥有自己的预印本服务器。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 自8月中旬起，936个AI智能体在封闭数字环境下进行长达12周的自主科研实验。这些智能体通过相互沟通、协作及撰写成果，模拟了复杂的人类科研生产流程。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Starting mid-August, a group of 936 AI agents conducted research in a closed digital environment over a 12-week period. The agents engaged in collaborative activities, information exchange, and report generation, simulating complex human scientific research workflows.
